items.verdict: only Evocation Wizards want it in combat; for everyone else it is a box-breaking looting convenience
action-neutral alone, but excellent when surrounded, and it doubles temp HP and flat damage reduction
turns off enemy healing with no save and blanks undead attack rolls; not the go-to damage cantrip
free thunder damage riding a normal weapon attack; once per action, so haste and Action Surge multiply it
needs a fresh corpse, clustered enemies and a failed DEX save; Acid Splash is usually better
spends concentration for light; the only real use is weighting poison-gas vents shut
best damage cantrip; separate attack rolls give reliability, crit chances and per-beam riders
highest raw damage for wizards and sorcerers, and it lights fires at 60 feet
advantage on Charisma checks; COUNTS AS A CRIME ON TACTICIAN AND HONOUR MODE, so hide or fast-travel afterwards
extra d4 on every ability check all game; he calls it the single most impactful spell
hands-free, concentration-free light lasting all day; most parties need some light source
costs a short-rest charge, but scouts, triggers traps, throws potions and soaks one enemy attack
moves NPCs with no save or roll; clusters enemies for AoE, sets ambushes, pulls enemies one at a time
worst damage type, worst save to target, and only 10-foot range; never the right pick
light plus a d8 ranged attack in one spell, but Toll the Dead supersedes it for clerics; CASTING UI BROKEN ON CONSOLE
movement debuff lets you kite as a stun, doubles on wet enemies, and freezes surfaces
d4 on saves; value is out of combat, on traps and dialogue saves you can see coming
Toll the Dead does more damage on a better save, so it has no role left after Patch 8
a d8 wisdom-based melee weapon makes early druids among the strongest melee combatants; he had badly underrated it before
melee-only on squishy casters; when you need it you should be spending a real resource instead
advantage on Intimidation and Performance only; Friends is better except that Thaumaturgy is not a crime
no-save 10-foot pull; repositions enemies off cliffs and back into Spike Growth
d12 on any damaged enemy at a WIS save; fixes early cleric damage, though wizards and warlocks skip it
an action for advantage is worse than attacking twice; only pre-combat or protecting a spent resource
too little damage to beat firing a bow; a late-game bard filler action only
